subject: Forensic extractability & retention schedule — Harbor Financial RFI
messages:
From: Paul Turner <paul.turner@harborfin.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Harbor Financial Legal <legal@harborfin.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: forensic extractability + retention schedule

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for picking up the RFI. Harbor Legal has a few targeted questions we need for our audit and regulatory team ahead of the procurement window. High-level asks below — we can follow with an intake call if you prefer.

1) For audit logs and user activity: what retention windows are configurable by account (hot, warm, archive)?
2) For a forensic request, what is the end-to-end timeline to produce a tamper-evident bulk extract (including checksums, chain-of-custody manifest, and delivery)?
3) What export formats do you support for full audit trails (schema + sample)? Are redaction options available before export?
4) Can you provide S3 delivery options and whether pre-signed links or direct upload to our bucket is supported?
5) Any SLAs for exports, and evidence of tamper-evidence processes (hashing, signatures)?

We are on a compressed timeline — the audit team would like answers and a sample extract by EOD next Tue (2028-04-18).

Appreciate it,
Paul
Paul Turner
Senior InfoSec Program Manager
Harbor Financial

---
(Attached: RFI intake template from Harbor: harbor_rfi_template.xlsx)

Thanks,

Paul / team — happy to provide the detailed answers and a sample. Summary below; attaching a short checklist (forensic-extract-checklist.xlsx) and the export spec we referenced earlier.

Short answers (details below):
- Retention windows: configurable by tenant with three tiers — Hot (0-90 days, low-latency access), Warm (91-365 days, slightly higher retrieval latency), Archive (>365 up to policy limit, cold storage). Customers can set custom retention policies at account level; default is Hot=90/Warm=275/Archive=indefinite unless contractually bounded.
- Export timeline: standard bulk export for audit logs (NDJSON/Parquet) is 48-72 hours from request acceptance for datasets < 10TB; expedited (24h) available with dedicated capacity add-on. Forensic snapshot (including chain-of-custody manifest, SHA256 checksums, and notarized timestamps) is typically 72-120 hours depending on data volume and legal hold complexity.
- Formats & redaction: we support NDJSON (line-delimited JSON), Parquet, and CSV exports. Redaction rules can be applied pre-export (PII redaction via retention/redaction policy) or we can deliver raw exports and a redaction map. Schema docs included in the Exportability_Spec_V1.pdf.
- Delivery: we support three delivery options — (1) pre-signed S3 PUT to your bucket, (2) Redwood direct upload to your S3 (cross-account role with customer-managed keys), (3) secure transfer to a customer-provided SFTP endpoint. Checksums (SHA256) and a signed manifest (chain-of-custody) are included with every export.
- Tamper evidence & integrity: all export files are hashed (SHA256), manifest signed with Redwood platform key, and we provide notarization timestamps (optional) and a Merkle-root summary for large multi-file exports. Audit logs include write timestamps and immutable event IDs; exports include the event ID mapping.

Detailed deliverables we will provide for your EOD-Tue sample:
- Small NDJSON sample (approx 10K events)
- Signed manifest.txt (file name, size, SHA256)
- Export schema + redaction map PDF
- Transfer instructions (pre-signed link example)

Note: For legal-preserved requests under litigation hold, we follow our preservation workflow which includes read-only snapshotting, internal access controls, and an evidence chain log that records every access to the export package.

Attaching: forensic-extract-checklist.xlsx (checklist + fields mapping).

Next steps: we can (a) send the sample as S3 pre-signed links by EOD Tue, or (b) schedule a 30-minute call on Tue morning to walk through the sample together. Which do you prefer?

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Security Solutions
Redwood Inference

1) Scope: for the sample, please limit to production audit logs for the last 12 months. We will request full-history extracts later if needed.
2) Delivery: pre-signed S3 PUTs to our bucket are preferred. We will provide bucket details and cross-account role if needed.
3) For the notarization step: can you share whether the notarization is a Redwood internal timestamp or via a third-party timestamping service? We need third-party proof where possible.

We would like the sample + manifest by EOD Tue (2028-04-18). If that works, please proceed and send the pre-signed URLs to me and legal@harborfin.com.

Paul

Paul — attaching the sample export and signed manifest as requested. Links and notes below.

Deliverables attached (sample stubs):
- sample-export-20280414.ndjson (10,512 events) — includes event_id, actor, timestamp, action, resource, request_id
- manifest-sample-20280414.txt (file list + sizes + SHA256)

We delivered via pre-signed S3 PUTs. Pre-signed URLs (60-minute expiry):
- https://redwood-presigned.s3.amazonaws.com/sample-export-20280414.ndjson (PRE-SIGNED URL, placeholder)
- https://redwood-presigned.s3.amazonaws.com/manifest-sample-20280414.txt (PRE-SIGNED URL, placeholder)

Notarization: we used a third-party timestamping authority (TSA) and included the TSA receipt in the manifest. The manifest includes the Merkle root, a platform signature, and the TSA receipt hash to prove third-party notarization.

Next steps:
- Please confirm receipt of the sample and that the file/manifest verify for your team.
- If acceptable, we can schedule a short call Mon morning to review the schema and redaction options for the full export scope.
- For legal transfer, we have a standard Data Transfer Addendum — I’ve created a DocuSign envelope for Harbor to sign: https://app.docusign.com/PLACEHOLDER/DocuSign-TDA-Harbor

Thanks — and happy to iterate quickly if you want additional fields in the sample.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Head of Security & Compliance Enablement
Redwood Inference
